solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Corrections said to be needed for manuscripts

indicators.note: said tells us the word is spoken, so we want a word that sounds like it

parts.note: rightings are acts of putting things right, i.e. corrections

explanation.surface: An editor insists that any handwritten drafts will need corrections.
explanation.definitionFit: Manuscripts are handwritten texts, and writings is a general name for such written works.

clue.text: Wise woman's repartee at church

parts.note: wit is quick, clever conversation, which is what repartee is

explanation.surface: A sage woman shows off her quick humour at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise woman' sounds complimentary, but it is an old name for one who practises magic.
explanation.definitionFit: A wise woman was a traditional term for a village healer or sorceress, i.e. one practising magic.

clue.text: Two minutes to crack one exam? Wicked!

indicators.note: to crack means to break into, so the minutes go inside the other letters

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
M is minute, so two of them give MM

explanation.surface: A student gets two minutes to break a single test, and exclaims in delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked!' reads as slang for great; it is the literal sense, sinful.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked in its literal sense means sinful or morally wrong.

clue.text: Additional folk joining in clarinet playing

indicators.note: joining in puts the folk inside the other letters
playing means the letters of clarinet are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, the instrument being played
men are people, folk

explanation.surface: Extra people join in as a clarinet is played.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incremental comes as an increase or extra step, so it is added on.

clue.text: Group of workers extremely lanky, ie this?

definitions.note: the clue points to the answer as meaning lanky

parts.note: a gang is a group of labourers

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extreme, outer letters of the word lanky

parts.note: the word whose outer letters are used

explanation.surface: A workers' gang that is very tall and thin.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back to 'lanky': the answer is what lanky means.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangly describes someone tall, thin and awkward in movement, so it means lanky.

clue.text: Small garden tool? It's over a foot

parts.note: a hoe is a long-handled tool for weeding

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a small garden tool that somehow ends up over a foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'over' meaning covering: a shoe sits over the foot, not measuring more than twelve inches.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear such as this is worn covering the foot, so it is literally placed over it.

clue.text: I must wear head covering, coming to one country

indicators.note: must wear means the I goes inside the head covering

parts.note: a hat covers the head
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to wear a hat on arriving in a foreign land.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is a nation in the Caribbean, so a country.

clue.text: Busy preparing for wedding

definitions.meaning: first meaning: occupied, as a phone line is
second meaning: betrothed, promised to marry

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone frantic with wedding plans; really the two phrases are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both occupied (a busy telephone) and betrothed with a marriage to come.

clue.text: Measure length of meal? Too long!

parts.note: to time something is to measure how long it lasts
consuming a meal is eating it; the question mark flags this loose sense

explanation.surface: Someone timing a dinner complains that it went on far too long.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as 'time the consuming', i.e. clock how long eating takes; the question mark admits that 'meal' stands loosely for eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that takes up an excessive amount of one's hours is said to be this, i.e. slow and lengthy.

clue.text: Suspected one may get wet here?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: being under suspicion, in disgrace
second meaning, a cryptic one: literally beneath a rain-bearing cloud

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for being under suspicion is taken literally in the second half: standing beneath a cloud you might be rained on.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone distrusted or in disgrace; literally it describes a spot beneath rain.

clue.text: Perhaps mount height, or both sides of slope

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: both sides means just the outer letters of the word slope, its first and last

parts.note: the word whose outer letters are used

explanation.surface: Choosing a mountaineering route: tackle the height, or go round the sides of the slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' reads as a mountain, but here it is something ridden; 'perhaps' marks a horse as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A mount is an animal one rides, and a horse is the commonest example of such a steed.

clue.text: Spooning out fish: youngster comes first

indicators.note: comes first says the youngster goes in front of the fish

parts.note: a lad is a boy
ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: At a fish supper, the child gets served first as the food is spooned out.
explanation.definitionFit: To ladle is to serve soup or stew with a large spoon, so this is serving with a scoop.

clue.text: I am inclined to announce girl's name

indicators.note: to announce is to speak aloud, so the spoken form is what counts

parts.note: I lean is another way of saying I am inclined

explanation.surface: Someone declares they are tempted to announce what a girl is called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclined' suggests a preference, but it works as tilting: I lean.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common female forename of Irish origin, so it fits a girl's name.

clue.text: Strange-looking creature concealed itself, covered in nasty acne

indicators.note: covered in means the concealing word sits inside the rearranged letters
nasty suggests disorder, so the letters of acne are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, the spots in the surface
hid means concealed itself

explanation.surface: An odd animal hides away, its face covered in spots.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny anteater of Australia is an egg-laying mammal of odd appearance.

clue.text: Stand journey, and make to return

parts.note: a trip is a journey

indicators.note: to return means the word for make is read backwards

parts.note: to do is to make, as in do a drawing

explanation.surface: An instruction to stand the journey and then head back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' looks like a verb meaning endure; it is the noun, a three-legged support.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged support for a camera or telescope is a kind of stand.

clue.text: Airborne soldier needs very large sunshade

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
so means very, as in so large

explanation.surface: A paratrooper requires an enormous umbrella against the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A light umbrella carried to shade one from the sun is a parasol.

clue.text: Board quickly reduced by US agency

indicators.note: reduced means the word for quickly is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: fast means quickly
the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: A company board is rapidly downsized by an American agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' suggests a company's directors; it is a plank, such as the one above a shop front.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascia is a flat plank, as found under eaves or over a shopfront carrying its name.

clue.text: Eight arranged in hotel area for meal

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters between the hotel and area letters
arranged means the letters of eight are put in a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Eight places have been set in the hotel lounge for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: H for hotel comes from the phonetic alphabet. This is a British early-evening meal with tea, often cooked food.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain this is a substantial early-evening meal served with tea, so a meal by definition.

clue.text: Noise from grand little pig

parts.note: the runt is the smallest piglet in a litter

explanation.surface: A sound coming from a big piglet.
explanation.walkthrough: G for grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars.
explanation.definitionFit: A grunt is a low guttural sound, especially one made by a pig.

clue.text: Woman vicar oligarch's protecting

indicators.note: protecting means the words wrap round and shelter the answer inside them

parts.note: the woman's name sits across the end of vicar and the start of oligarch's

explanation.surface: A rich oligarch is shielding a female member of the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman' looks like a description of the vicar, but it defines a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female forename, so the clue uses woman to point to a name borne by women.

clue.text: Behold, by study, waterproof cloth

parts.note: lo is an archaic exclamation meaning look, behold
a den is a private room for working

explanation.surface: Look, there's waterproof fabric beside the study.
explanation.definitionFit: Loden is a thick waterproof woollen fabric from the Tyrol, used for coats.

clue.text: Twice walked over, being cheated

definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken literally: crossed two times
second meaning: betrayed by someone feigning loyalty

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the word literally, crossed twice over; 'being' simply links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To be betrayed by someone pretending to be on your side is to be swindled, so the idiom fits.

clue.text: A court ultimately enforces decisions of Parliament

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the word enforces is taken

parts.note: the word whose final letter is used

explanation.surface: A court in the end puts Parliament's rulings into effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Laws passed by a legislature are known by this name, as in an Act of Parliament.

clue.text: Badly mangled a college's name

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put together wrongly, so they are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone has badly mispronounced the name of a college.
explanation.walkthrough: Magdalen is a college at Oxford, famously pronounced 'maudlin', which is why mangling its name is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford University has a college with this name, so it is a college's title.
